record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Let CSL be the comparative-similarity language whose basic closer operator closer(tau1,tau2) is interpreted at a point x as true exactly when the distance from x to the extension of tau1 is smaller than the distance from x to the extension of tau2. For various classes of distance or metric models, provide axiomatisations of the CSL formulas valid in those classes.

artifact.status_search_result: An axiomatisation of CSL over minspaces (distance spaces in which the relevant infima are attained) has been given by Alenda, Olivetti and Schwind, with accompanying tableaux calculi extended to arbitrary distance spaces and to triangular/metric models. However, complete finite axiomatisations of CSL over the full classes of metric spaces and of Euclidean spaces appear not to have been established, and undecidability/complexity results (via tree automata and Diophantine equations) suggest substantial obstacles. The general problem therefore appears only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Comparative concept similarity over Minspaces: Axiomatisation and Tableaux Calculus
status_evidence.snippet: A direct axiomatisation of this logic over minspaces is given, together with a decision procedure in the form of a tableaux calculus.
status_evidence.claim: Axiomatisation is known for the minspace fragment.

status_evidence.title: Tableau Calculus for the Logic of Comparative Similarity over Arbitrary Distance Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Tableau calculus over arbitrary distance spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Proof systems extended beyond minspaces, but axiomatic completeness for metric/Euclidean classes not settled.

status_evidence.title: Comparative Similarity, Tree Automata, and Diophantine Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Connections to tree automata and Diophantine equations indicate high complexity / undecidability for metric variants.
status_evidence.claim: Suggests the general axiomatisation problem for metric classes remains hard/open.
